text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for Private Inference Gateway (multiple customers) starting ~2026-03-14T03:12:00Z — spike in 502/504s and connection resets. Alert details: 30m rolling error rate > 7% for private-gw-prod clusters.

bob_oncall: ack'ing. I'm oncall now, pinging netops and eng. assigning sev=P1 until we triage.

alice_netops: looking. which regions/customers affected? any correlated change events?

bob_oncall: multi-region but concentrated in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Affected customers: ACME (private), NovaHealth (private), internal e2e tests. No obvious deploys from deploy-bot at 03:10-03:20.

deploy-bot: no infra deploys in that window. latest infra apply was 02:40 UTC.

carol_sre: grabbing gateway logs + lb traces. early sign: backend connections are being reset from upstream (reset by peer) causing 502s. I'll start a tcpdump on a symptomatic host.

carol_sre: tcpdump snippet (sanitized):
```
12:31:58.123456 IP 10.0.5.21.52344 > 10.10.2.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:31:58.123459 IP 10.10.2.11.443 > 10.0.5.21.52344: Flags [S.], seq 0
12:31:58.124000 IP 10.0.5.21.52344 > 10.10.2.11.443: Flags [R], seq 1 ack 1 
```
packets show connection reset immediately after SYN-ACK.

alice_netops: that's suspicious — resets consistent with asymmetric return path or middlebox dropping flows. Checking TGW and route table events.

alice_netops: CloudTrail/CloudWatch shows Transit Gateway attachment tgw-attach-0a1b2c toggled (detached/attached) at 03:12:05-03:16:30 in us-west-2. Also see route propagation removed briefly from the VPC route table.

dave_eng: did anything touch the third-party firewall appliance or on-prem peering at that time?

alice_netops: automated config job touched firewall appliance cluster just before 03:12 — we have a conflicting HA failover on the appliance that coincided. The appliance removed route propagation to the TGW during HA switchover, leading to asymmetric forwarding for return packets.

bob_oncall: so traffic goes out via the TGW -> appliance -> internet, return traffic comes back via different TGW attachment because propagation missing, net result: connection resets.

carol_sre: confirmed via traceroute from gw-host: outbound path -> tgw-attach-A -> appliance -> nat-gw; inbound syn-ack arrives via tgw-attach-B, appliance drops it because flow table missing -> reset.

bob_oncall: mitigation plan — we need to re-establish symmetric routes ASAP. Options: 1) re-enable route propagation on affected route tables (fast) 2) temporarily shift the private-gw subnets to an alternate route that bypasses the appliance (nv1) 3) provision per-AZ NAT GW to stop TGW path for egress. Which is fastest?

alice_netops: re-enable propagation now. Doing a small route apply to re-add propagated routes to the VPC RTs. Executing: `aws ec2 enable-transit-gateway-route-table-propagation --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0abcd --transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-0a1b2c`

alice_netops: propagation re-enabled at 03:20:45 UTC.

carol_sre: error rate dropping in 1 minute after propagation — 502s falling from 8% -> 0.8% in us-west-2. tcpdump shows syn-ack now followed by established flows.

bob_oncall: good. moving to mitigation-complete for now. Leaving P1 open until we confirm stable for 30m and run postmortem.

emma_csm: I'll draft a customer-facing note. Short one: "We experienced brief elevated gateway errors for customers using Private Inference Gateway in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 between 03:12-03:20 UTC. Root cause identified as a transit gateway route propagation interruption linked to a third-party firewall HA switchover; traffic returned to normal after route propagation was reenabled. We will follow up with detailed RCA and mitigations." Sound ok?

dave_eng: adding follow-ups: 1) add TGW-attachment health alerts to platform monitoring (watch for attach/detach). 2) add runbook step to block automation jobs from triggering firewall HA during business hours or coordinate. 3) evaluate per-AZ NAT fallback for private-gw customers to avoid single appliance causing asymmetric routing. 4) postmortem and customer RCA.

carol_sre: also adding a quick detector: monitor for immediate TCP RSTs within 100ms of SYN-ACKs from our backends — fast signal of asymmetric path.

bob_oncall: thanks all. I'll hand to the morning oncall in 20m with status update. tagging next oncall: @alice_netops will be lead for remediation and postmortem.

alice_netops: accepted. I'll own the RCA write-up and timeline. Initial root cause: TGW attachment briefly lost route propagation due to firewall HA switchover causing asymmetric routing and dropped return packets -> 502/504 for private-gw. Scope: affected customers on Private Inference over peered/appliance paths in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; incident duration approx 8 minutes.

bob_oncall: done for now. leaving channel open for any follow-up. :thumbsup:
